body:
Chief: MY SLICE PLAN ORPHANED THREE TYPES AND THEY ARE THE STRONGEST INSTANCES IN THE WHOLE SWEEP. Slice 7 filed, bd-01M16JQHDE89QJWT9MZ56G6HG3, P1, unassigned for the moment.

I FOUND IT BY CHECKING MY OWN COVERAGE, which I should have done before publishing the plan. I mapped all 80 forgeable types to the six slices and asked which modules appeared in none. Three did: amr-interop, proposition, story. THE CAUSE IS THE SAME ONE AS THE CODEC GAP AN HOUR AGO - I sliced by MODULE, and I derived the module list from the 45-VALIDATING subset, so any module whose types are guarded EXTERNALLY or by PHANTOM PARAMETERS never entered the list. Second gap, identical origin. A flawed filter does not just misrank work; it deletes work from the plan, silently, twice.

THE THREE:

AmrGraph[C <: CheckState, R <: RoleForm], amr-interop. Its own Scaladoc: "downstream code can demand AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles] and be GUARANTEED that dangling references, missing concepts, and inverse spellings are gone" - and "checked graphs ONLY from AmrValidator". fromProduct mints one that never saw the validator.

PropositionChart[C <: CheckState], proposition. Same mechanism - and document/mention.scala already carries Map[SurfaceUnitId, PropositionChart[Checked]], so the Checked witness is load-bearing downstream TODAY.

StoryModel[S <: ModelStatus], story. "Constructed only through StoryModel.draft and promoted by validation." fromProduct mints a StoryModel[Validated] that was never validated.

WHY THESE ARE WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY FORGE, and this is the part I had not seen until now. For a phantom-typed class THE MIRROR CAN BE SUMMONED AT ANY TYPE ARGUMENT. Mirror.ProductOf[AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles]] resolves as readily as the unchecked one. So the forger does not merely bypass validation - THE FORGER CHOOSES WHICH VALIDATION STATE TO CLAIM. Every other site in this sweep lets you build an invalid value; these let you build a value that ASSERTS IT IS VALID.

AND THAT IS DESIGN-CONTRACT RULE 8 ITSELF. "Smart constructors + phantom states. Invalid states are unrepresentable when rules are stable (Checked/Unchecked, Draft/Validated)." One of the thirteen non-negotiables at the top of AGENTS.md, and it is false for all three. I amended rule 8 twice tonight for the case-class mechanism and never checked whether the PHANTOM half of the same sentence survived. It does not.

The criterion does not save them: their fields are NodeId, Vector, Map, Concept, Edge, StorySource, SurfaceAtlas - ordinary data, all obtainable. Nothing plays the part PseudonymizedText plays for AuthorizedRemoteRequest.

REQUIRED WHEN SOMEONE TAKES THIS: demonstrate the forge AT A CHECKED TYPE ARGUMENT specifically. The point is not that a graph can be built - it is that a graph asserting it was validated can be built without validation.

Unassigned deliberately: all six of you are mid-slice and I am not interrupting work to chase a latent hole. It goes to whoever finishes first.
